sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic) with significant Common Law influence in commercial, trust, and foundation practice
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States-Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (2012, Investment Chapter)
Panama-Republic of Korea Double Taxation Agreement (2022)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Private Interest Foundations: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (as amended by Law 41 of 2016 and Law 3 of 2021). AML/CFT: Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 (as amended by Law 70 of 2019) and Executive Decree No. 363 of 2013. UBO Register: Law No. 129 of 16 November 2020 and Executive Decree No. 53 of 2021, creating the Registro Unico de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF) administered by the Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI). Supervisory guidance: SBR Resolution No. 015-2021 and UAF on-site inspection program.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Legal Existence (for corporate founders)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory identification of Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) under Law 23 of 2015 (as amended) and Article 31 of Executive Decree 363 of 2013. The resident agent must screen all founders and UBOs against the OFAC SDN List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Sanctions List, and Panama's domestic sanctions designations. PEP status requires enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and continuous monitoring of source of funds. All UBOs are screened at onboarding and periodically thereafter under the foundation's risk-based compliance policy.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Publico de Panama (Public Registry of Panama) - online consultation and reservation via the Sistema de Informacion y Gestion Registral (SIAG) at www.registropublico.gob.pa. Foundation name availability is verified by registry certificate; Panama Emprende applies only to commercial companies and municipal permits.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A foundation name may be expressed in any language using a Latin-script transliteration of non-Latin alphabets. Spanish prevails for registry indexing and legal interpretation; the Registry requires a distinguishable name that does not replicate or imitate any existing registered corporation, association, or foundation. Bilingual Spanish/English Foundation Charters are standard market practice.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Identical or confusingly similar names of existing registered legal entities (Article 10, Law 25 of 1995)
Banco / Bank - requires prior Superintendencia de Bancos (SBR) authorization
Seguros / Insurance / Reaseguros - requires prior Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros (SSRP) authorization
Fondo de Inversion / Investment Fund / Valores - requires prior Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores (SMV) authorization
Trust / Fideicomiso - requires prior registry approval
Cooperativa / Mutual / Asociacid de Ahorro - restricted terms requiring sectoral approval
Names suggesting government sponsorship: Gobierno, Ministerio, Estado, Nacional, Municipal
Names of international organizations: ONU, Cruz Roja, UNESCO, OMS, including acronyms
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registry rejects the proposed name, it issues a written notification citing the conflicting registration. Applicant may file a 'recurso de apelacion' before the Direccion General del Registro Publico within 5 business days of notification under Law 38 of 2000. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately resubmit with a modified, distinguishable name. A valid reservation lapses after 30 days and may be renewed for one additional 30-day period at the Registry's discretion; after lapse, the name becomes available to third parties.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted. A Private Interest Foundation must maintain a registered office at the address of its Panamanian resident agent (a licensed attorney or notary under Article 13 of Law 25 of 1995). No physical business premises are statutorily required for the foundation itself when the ISIC 4791 subscription box operations, warehousing, and fulfillment are conducted abroad. If the foundation directly performs physical storage or local distribution within Panama, a municipal Aviso de Operacion and a physical address may become mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: low for the foundation itself - approximately 2-5% annual probability of unannounced physical inspection for a low-risk, non-licensed subscription box holding structure. The resident agent, however, carries a 10-20% annual probability of inspection under the UAF's on-site AML/CFT inspection program.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Law No. 41 of 2013 and governed by Executive Decree No. 15 of 2017; Articles 8 (content of the foundation charter), 13 (registered office and resident agent), and 24 (Foundation Council)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Mercantile Section – Foundations Desk
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Carta Fundacional), executed as a public deed (Escritura Pública) before a Panamanian Notary Public and inscribed in the Public Registry
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Foundation Charter must allocate an initial endowment (patrimonio inicial) of at least US$10,000 under Article 8 of Law No. 25 of 1995. Panama does not mandate an escrow account for a Private Interest Foundation; the endowment is evidenced by the founder's asset inventory recorded in the Charter, and no capital deposit certificate is required for registry inscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL RESOLVES, EFFECTIVE IMMEDIATELY: FIRST, that the initial endowment of US$10,000 is accepted, receipt being acknowledged, and recorded in the asset inventory. SECOND, that the registered office of the Foundation is established at the offices of the Resident Agent, Panama City, Republic of Panama. THIRD, that [Name] is appointed President, [Name] is appointed Secretary, and [Name] is appointed Treasurer of the Foundation Council. FOURTH, that the President is authorized to file the Foundation Charter with the Public Registry of Panama, procure certified copies, and execute all ancillary instruments. FIFTH, that the Foundation adopts as its purpose subscription-based merchandising of physical goods under ISIC 4791, and confirms the retention of the Resident Agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Retention of Licensed Resident Agent and AML/KYC Intake
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian Resident Agent (attorney or fiduciary licensed by the Registro Público de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute an engagement letter appointing a resident agent duly authorized to represent Private Interest Foundations. Deliver beneficial ownership information and supporting documentation required by Law No. 32 of 2011 and the Registry's due diligence regulations. Confirm the proposed foundation name is available through the Public Registry's name check process.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Founder's passport
Proof of residential address of the Founder and beneficiaries (utility bill or bank statement)
Draft Foundation Charter and asset inventory of initial endowment
Beneficial ownership and KYC declaration (Law No. 32 of 2011)
Engagement letter appointing the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Name reservation rejections are cured by resubmitting an alternative foundation name in a supplementary reservation request; eligibility objections to the resident agent are remedied by appointing a substitute licensed agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Review, and Notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public authorized to practice in the Republic of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the Charter text including foundation name, object, duration, initial endowment, asset inventory, composition of the Foundation Council, protector provisions, beneficiary clauses, and applicable law. Execute the instrument as a public deed (Escritura Pública) before the notary, pay notarial fees, and obtain the notarial protocol and copies required for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Final Foundation Charter text
Founder's passport and capacity documentation
Signed inventory of assets forming the initial endowment
Notarial appointment sheet (carátula)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a query on any clause, revise the draft through legal counsel and reschedule execution; defective signatures are cured by re-signature before the same notary without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Foundation Charter in the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Mercantile Section, Foundations Desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized original protocol and two plain copies, together with the inscription petition signed by the resident agent. Pay the inscription tax and registry fees. The Registry verifies compliance with Law No. 25 of 1995, including the US$10,000 endowment reference and the registered agent clause, and issues the certificate of inscription.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Charter (original protocol)
Two plain copies of the Foundation Charter
Petition for inscription signed by the Resident Agent
Proof of payment of Public Registry inscription fees
Copy of the Resident Agent engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect notice (nota de defecto), cure the observations within 10 business days; an adverse denial may be challenged by a reconsideration petition before the Director General of the Public Registry, and re-filing as a new presentation is available if the cure period lapses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Procurement of Certified Registry Copy and Banking Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Certified Copies Desk); licensed Panamanian bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request a certified copy (copia certificada) of the registered Foundation Charter and certified evidence of appointment of the Foundation Council. Use these instruments to open the foundation's bank account, complete banking KYC, and register authorized signatories for subscription revenue collection.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscribed Foundation Charter
Certificate of appointment of Foundation Council members
Registry-issued record of inscription (certificado de registro)
Bank KYC forms and source-of-funds declarations
Passport copies of the authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank documentation queries within the requested deadline; additional apostilled documents are obtained through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and alternative banking institutions may be approached if an account application is declined.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with DGI and Municipal Operating Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministry of Economy and Finance; Municipality of Panama – Revenue Directorate (Dirección de Rentas Municipales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Foundation in the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) and obtain the tax identification number. If the Foundation maintains physical premises in Panama, file the Aviso de Operación and obtain the municipal tax receipt (patente). Under Panama's territorial tax system, foreign-source subscription box revenue is not subject to Panamanian income tax; local logistics, warehousing, and ancillary services trigger applicable VAT and municipal charges.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscribed Foundation Charter
Passport copies of Foundation Council members
Resident Agent designation letter
DGI RUC application form (Form 328 series)
Lease contract or ownership title of premises (if physical operations)
Municipal Aviso de Operación application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to DGI fiscal verification requests (vistas) within 10 business days; municipal zoning or documentation objections are cured by correcting lease or occupancy documents and resubmitting the Aviso de Operación application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Operational, Fire-Safety, Occupational, and Environmental Clearances (Physical Fulfillment Only)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cuerpo de Bomberos de la República de Panamá; Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE); Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL); Ministry of Health (MINSA) for regulated consumer goods
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Undergo fire-safety inspection of the warehouse and obtain the Fire Safety Operating Permit. Register the facility with MiAMBIENTE under Category I environmental registration. Submit the occupational health and safety workplace dossier to MITRADEL. Secure the MINSA sanitary operating permit if the subscription boxes contain foods, cosmetics, hygiene products, or other regulated goods.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement and floor plan of the warehouse
Certificate of occupancy and structural certification
Fire inspection request and evacuation plan
MiAMBIENTE Category I environmental registration form and waste management plan
MITRADEL workplace safety plan
MINSA product safety data sheets for regulated product categories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct all non-conformities identified in the official inspection report and resubmit within the stated remediation period; administrative denials may be appealed to the respective administrative tribunal within 30 days of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No special industrial license applies to ISIC 4791 subscription box merchandising in Panama. Conditional operational permits are administered by the Municipality of Panama (Aviso de Operación and patente), the Ministry of Health (MINSA sanitary permit for regulated consumer goods), and the Cuerpo de Bomberos de la República de Panamá (fire safety permit for premises).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Conditional Aviso de Operación (Municipal Operating Notice); MINSA Sanitary Operating Permit; Fire Safety Operating Permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – National Directorate of Environmental Impact Assessment and Environmental Compliance
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Environmental Registration (Registro Ambiental) applies to low-impact warehousing, pick-and-pack, and distribution facilities; a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Report is not required. Purely virtual operations using third-party drop-ship fulfillment may qualify as exempt from environmental permitting, subject to MiAMBIENTE's written confirmation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary wastewater discharges must comply with receiving-water quality standards under Executive Decree No. 75 of 2013 and the regulations of Law No. 41 of 1998; connection to the municipal sewerage system or an approved on-site treatment unit is mandatory. Solid waste, including cardboard, plastic packaging, and other recyclables, must be source-separated and transported by licensed municipal haulers. Air and VOC emissions from cleaning and packaging operations are negligible, but the facility must remain compliant with national ambient air quality standards and the prohibition on ozone-depleting substances under Law No. 29 of 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Operating Permit issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de la República de Panamá following on-site inspection of fire exits, extinguishers, hydrants, and emergency lighting; structural and load-capacity clearance of warehouse mezzanines and racking systems certified by a licensed structural engineer; and an Occupational Health and Safety workplace clearance from MITRADEL covering accident-prevention plans, first-aid equipment, employee training, and general industrial hygiene per Panamanian workplace regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) — official portal: https://dgi.mef.gob.pa (e-services: Sede Electrónica)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) or any foreign entity with a Panamanian tax nexus, the statutory tax identification number is the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente). The DGI registration is conducted via the Sede Electrónica de la DGI (online portal). Steps: (1) submit the notarized and legalized/apostilled Certificate of Incorporation (Acta de Constitución), and for foreign entities, proof of registration in the home jurisdiction; (2) designate a resident legal representative (agente residente) with a Panama address; (3) complete the electronic Form RUC-01, stating the entity's business purpose and legal form; (4) attest to the territorial source characterization of income; (5) provide supporting documentation for value-chain activities; (6) the DGI verifies the information and issues the provisional RUC within 5 to 10 business days. Non-resident entities without a permanent establishment may alternatively request a non-resident TIN for withholding tax purposes via the same portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a check-the-box election regime. Entity classification follows the legal form and the territorial source rules. A PIF can elect to be organized for either non-commercial or qualified commercial purposes; the latter subjects it to normal income tax and ITBMS obligations for Panamanian-source activities. Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognized. Consolidated taxation is available only to related corporations under specific conditions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Corporales Muebles y Servicios, ITBMS)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 (equivalent to USD 36,000) in annual gross taxable sales; annual transactions below this threshold are exempt from VAT registration unless voluntarily registered.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama operates a compulsory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) regime for businesses designated by the DGI. The system requires real-time fiscal authorization: every invoice must be validated and an authorization code obtained via the DGI web service or an authorized fiscal printer before issuance. Taxpayers must integrate their ERP or billing systems with the DGI API to submit electronic transactions, and attach a digital stamp (Código QR) to PDF or printed invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of physical goods leaving Panamanian territory and services performed abroad or rendered to non-residents (with limited exceptions) are zero-rated (0%) for ITBMS. The exporter must hold a valid RUC, be compliant with electronic invoicing, issue an export invoice reflecting zero rate, and transfer the goods out of the customs territory within 30 days of invoicing. Certification by the customs authority (Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas de Panamá) is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación de Aduanas)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (Conocimiento de Embarque)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing foreign revenue receipt (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI conducts substantive audits of exported invoices and import/export matching. Fraudulent zero-rating claims are subject to retroactive recovery of the tax plus surcharges (average official interest rate plus 10%) and fines of 100% to 200% of the tax underpaid. Directors and representatives may be subject to criminal tax fraud liability under Panama's Tax Criminal Law (Ley 20 of 2018).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: There is no central bank in the Republic of Panama. The Republic is fully dollarized with U.S. dollars serving as legal tender; banking and foreign-exchange operations are supervised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The U.S. dollar is the national currency and there are no exchange controls. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible for legal entities, including Private Interest Foundations. Profit and dividend repatriation to non-resident founders/beneficiaries is unrestricted. Panama applies a territorial tax system; however, if a PIF directly carries on a Panama-source commercial activity, including subscription merchandising delivered to or managed from Panama, Panama-source income may be subject to ISR (Corporate Income Tax) at 25%, while foreign-source revenue remains outside the taxable base subject to proper records.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion exists. Export invoices may be denominated in USD, Latin American currencies, or EUR; proceeds may remain offshore, be credited to Panama bank accounts, or be applied for outbound supplier settlements without any obligation to convert into local currency. Panamanian monetary law requires only that bank accounting be expressed in USD.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with material legal constraints. Panama has no comprehensive electronic-money-institution (EMI) licensing regime analogous to the EU/UK PSD2; offshore EMI accounts (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) are usable as collection/disbursement rails but are not recognized as full bank deposits and may be de-risked by SBP-regulated banks. Ongoing balances must sweep to a Panamanian bank account. Use of EMIs requires contractual evidence of platform ownership and verified KYC data flowing to the PIF's registered agent and bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Generally mandatory. At least one duly appointed foundation council member or protector must appear physically before the bank's compliance officer for the initial KYC interview; bank officers also make verification calls to the registered agent. Remote opening is accepted only in exceptional, low-risk renewals after the initial physical onboarding has been completed, and requires apostilled notarial powers and a registered-agent certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity in the Private Interest Foundation structure (registered-agent nominee patterns and non-resident beneficiaries).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authentic foundation deed (Acta de Fundación) and regulations; current sworn declaration of the foundation council identifying all founders, council members, protectors, and beneficiaries; certificate of beneficial owner filing issued under Panama's Law 23 of 2015 / unified register records; notarized and apostilled identity documents and proof of current address for all ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection or founder contribution without clear source of funds and business purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foundation deed article containing the exact endowment contribution; founder's source-of-funds certificate from a licensed bank or asset/portfolio statement; certified transfer instructions; updated annual statement from the registered agent; PIF resolution showing board approval of the injected amount as irrevocable patrimony, not a loan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency recurring subscription-box revenue collected via Stripe/Braintree channels causing e-commerce aggregation flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Stripe Billing merchant-of-record agreement; platform dashboard with transactional history; refund and chargeback policy; consumer contract/terms of subscription; resolution of foundation council designating authorized signatories for treasury reconciliation; PDF report of the recurring billing ledger with settlement dates mapped to the Panama bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of economic substance given a tax-neutral PIF is ultimately involved in a physical goods commerce chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office lease in Panama; minutes of foundation council meetings evidencing active management of the subscription business; copies of supplier contracts and shipping/customs records; Panama RUC (tax identification) and municipal operating license if applicable; annual tax returns declaring territorial income if any.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound wires to the PIF's Panama operational account must be sent via SWIFT MT103 (or MT202 COV for interbank transfers) in USD to the beneficiary bank; the message must include the beneficiary legal name exactly as registered, the foundation document number, and the transaction narrative: 'Subscription merchandise e-commerce settlement / capital contribution under Foundation Deed [date]'. No FX conversion is required in Panama for USD. The receiving bank will verify against the account-opening file; supporting evidence includes the executed foundation deed contribution clause, settlement reconciliation statement from Stripe/Braintree, and a notarized council resolution if beneficial owner changes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for subscription-box inventory should be executed by SWIFT MT103 (gpi with UETR) for suppliers requiring wire settlement; by documentary commercial letters of credit (sight or 30–180 day usance) for bulk cross-border inventory from Asia/Latin America; and by book transfer or local clearing for Panama domestic vendors. Use SWIFT gpi through Banco General/Banistmo correspondent networks; all payments to related or overseas suppliers require apostilled supplier contract, commercial invoice, proof of delivery (B/L/AWB), and a matching purchase order.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable forwards between USD and EUR/GBP for subscription-pricing receipts with maximum tenor 12 months.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referenced to selected Latin American currencies (COP, MXN, BRL) for invoicing to regional customers; underlying commercial exposure must be demonstrated.
Cross-currency swaps for longer-term supply agreements (2+ years) with SBP-licensed counterparties and board-approved maturity-exposure limits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Franchise Tax Payment (Pago del Impuesto Anual de Franquicia de la Fundación)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos, Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than March 15 of each calendar year; no grace period is granted by the Revenue Code.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues a monthly surcharge of 10% (up to a maximum of 50%) plus statutory interest at 9% per annum. Persistent non-payment for two consecutive years triggers administrative suspension of the Foundation's legal rights and the eventual strike-off of the Foundation from the Public Registry of Panama.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Register Update (Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Beneficial Ownership Registry, through the Licensed Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of the Foundation's initial registration, and within 30 days after any change in founder, beneficiary, foundation council, or economic interest.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing of a beneficial ownership update subjects the Foundation to fines of USD 1,000 to USD 10,000, suspension of the Foundation's title certificates, and eventual administrative strike-off for repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Retention of Statutory Accounting and Corporate Records Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Office / Resident Agent, Panama Public Registry oversight
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Books and registers must remain physically available at the registered office for immediate inspection on the anniversary date of the Foundation; no filing is made with the Public Registry unless a register audit is requested.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain complete statutory registers on site can result in the registered agent's license being sanctioned and the Foundation being deemed non-compliant for tax domicile purposes; repeat violations lead to suspension of the Foundation's registered status in Panama.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit is imposed on a Private Interest Foundation under Law 25 of 1995 solely because of its PIF status. A compulsory independent certified audit is triggered only if: (i) the Foundation is designated a public-interest entity under Panamanian securities or banking law; (ii) the Foundation Charter expressly requires an audit; (iii) the Foundation holds assets or generates revenue in Panama that makes it taxable and audited financial statements are required for tax assessment; or (iv) a third-party creditor or beneficiary validly obtains a court-ordered audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) is required for public-interest entities. A Private Interest Foundation may otherwise maintain books under Panama Local GAAP (Normas de Información Financiera de Panamá) or another internationally recognised framework expressly designated in the Foundation Charter.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Foundation must maintain a current Beneficial Owner Register (Registro de Beneficiario Final) in accordance with Law 25 of 1995, as amended by Law 70 of 2017. The licensed Resident Agent must obtain an annual written confirmation from the Foundation Council that the roster of founders, foundation council members, guardians, and beneficial interests exceeds the public threshold or otherwise is accurately disclosed. Any transfer or modification of an economic interest must be reflected in the Register within 30 days and, where required, the agent must present the corresponding update to the Panama Public Registry. The Foundation is not subject to a shareholders' annual meeting obligation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners (Registro de Beneficiario Final)
Register of Foundation Council Resolutions (Actas de Consejo de la Fundación)
Register of Economic Interests / Beneficiaries (Registro de Intereses Económicos)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 to USD 800 per annum for a Panama licensed resident agent and registered office for a Private Interest Foundation
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 to USD 6,000 for a certified independent audit of a Panama Private Interest Foundation when a statutory or charter-triggered audit applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (top marginal rate on taxable income exceeding USD 1,500,000; progressive brackets: 10% on the first USD 50,000 and 15% on USD 50,001–1,500,000)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: foreign-source income is exempt from Panamanian corporate income tax. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) under Law 25 of 1995 is tax-neutral on foundation assets and on proceeds derived from activities performed and revenues generated outside Panama. Subscription box e-commerce revenues from non-Panamanian subscribers processed via Stripe Billing or Authorize.Net are generally 0% Panamanian CIT because the economic activity occurs abroad. Only Panamanian-source revenue (sales to Panama-based subscribers, local warehousing, or local logistics operations) is subject to CIT at the progressive 10%/15%/25% rates. No sector-specific tax holiday applies to ISIC 4791; the effective rate on a profitable domestic Panamanian e-commerce operation is approximately 10% to 15%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 42 (Declaración de Renta) — Corporate Income Tax Return filed through the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) E-Tax 2.0 electronic filing system (www.dgi.gob.pa).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (standard fiscal year ends 31 December; monthly advance income tax payments are due during the year and reconciled on the annual return)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: On or before 31 March of the year following the close of the fiscal year (within 3 months after fiscal year-end for non-calendar fiscal years). A PIF must file even if all income is foreign-source and no tax is due, or file a zero/surveillance declaration where required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The foundation's 10-digit Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC) number issued by the DGI upon registration and fiscal activation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident founder must appoint and maintain a Panama-licensed resident agent and a fiscal representative to obtain and operate the RUC; all filings are made under the PIF's RUC and the resident agent's liability is engaged.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Elected fiscal year (typically 1 January to 31 December). A PIF may elect a different year-end with DGI prior approval.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners should align the PIF's fiscal year with the last consolidated financial statements of the subscription-box business to simplify transfer pricing documentation and DTA residence certifications.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 3 — Ingresos Brutos de Fuente Panameña
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from sources inside Panama, including subscription fees from Panama-based customers, local warehouse sales, and services rendered or used within Panamanian territory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Panamanian-subscriber receipts and locally delivered subscription box sales are reportable. Cross-border e-commerce sales to foreign subscribers are excluded from this line under the territoriality principle; the PIF must retain subscriber location and shipping documentation to support the source classification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Informational disclosure of foreign-source receipts, including subscription fees from non-Panamanian customers, international card payments processed by Stripe Billing and Authorize.Net, and income from foreign logistics providers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source income is exempt but must be declared in the supporting schedules to substantiate the 0% effective tax rate. The non-resident PIF must avoid any Panamanian management, warehousing, or fulfillment activity that could re-source the income to Panama; income-sourcing documentation must show that contracting, payment processing, and delivery decisions occur outside Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record allowable deductions strictly attributable to Panamanian-source gross income: cost of goods sold, freight and customs, merchant fees, marketing, salaries of Panama-based staff, and allocable general administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses attributable to foreign-source subscription revenue are not deductible against Panamanian-source income and must be allocated using a consistent, documented ratio. The PIF must maintain invoices, clearing reports from Stripe and Authorize.Net, and transfer pricing documentation for intercompany cost allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income equal to Panamanian-source gross revenue less allowable deductions, before applying the progressive rate brackets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PIF's Panama-based activities are limited to passive contract signing and the subscription boxes are sold and delivered exclusively abroad, taxable income may be zero; a supporting legal memorandum and physical substance record should be retained to withstand DGI challenge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax calculated by applying 10% on the first USD 50,000 of taxable income, 15% on USD 50,001 to USD 1,500,000, and 25% above USD 1,500,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the non-resident PIF with zero Panamanian-source income, the computed tax is zero; no minimum tax (anticipo mínimo) or CAIR (Complemento al Impuesto de Renta) applies unless gross Panamanian-source income exceeds the statutory threshold; a formal zero-return with schedules is still required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 8 — Retenciones, Anticipos y Saldo a Pagar
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for withholding taxes paid by Panamanian customers, monthly advance payments (pagos mensuales), and the resulting final tax payable or refundable balance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PIF must reconcile any Panamanian withholding certificates (Formulario de Retención) and advance payments made by its resident agent; foreign taxes withheld by Stripe or other payment processors are not creditable against Panamanian CIT unless a treaty provision so provides.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 42 attracts a monthly surcharge of 5% of the tax due (capped at 50%) under Article 758 of the Fiscal Code, plus monthly interest of 1% on late payments. Additional administrative fines range from USD 50 to USD 10,000 per unfiled or defective return. Persistent non-filing triggers RUC suspension, seizure of local bank accounts, criminal referral under Law 66 of 2017, and travel restrictions against the resident agent and foundation council.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% standard Panama withholding tax on dividend distributions made by a Panamanian entity out of Panamanian-source taxable profits; 5% applies where the distributed profits have been fully subject to Panamanian corporate income tax at the gross-up standard rate. Dividends paid by a PIF out of foreign-source subscription-box profits are not subject to Panamanian withholding tax because such profits fall outside Panama's territorial tax net.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's double tax treaty network includes Mexico, Singapore, South Korea, UAE, Qatar, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Spain, Italy, France, Portugal, and other OECD-aligned partners. To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner must: (i) obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the DGI, (ii) complete the DGI treaty-relief application (Form 41 or successor form) and submit it together with the TRC and a beneficial-ownership declaration, (iii) obtain prior DGI approval or retain the documentation for clearance at payment time, and (iv) maintain the distribution records in Panama for 5 years. Treaty-reduced dividend rates (typically 5%–10%, often 0% for certain holdings) apply only where the non-resident holder has real economic substance and meets the treaty's limitation-on-benefits provisions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 12.5% statutory Panama withholding tax on gross royalties paid for the use of trademarks, patents, software, and IP in Panama; DTA-reduced rates of 5%–10% may apply under applicable treaties (e.g., Mexico, Singapore, Netherlands). Interest: Panama does not levy withholding tax on interest paid to non-resident lenders where the loan funds are used outside Panama; interest sourced to Panamanian collateral or Panamanian economic usage may fall within territorial taxation and be subject to a 5%–12.5% withholding, subject to treaty reduction to 5% or 0% in many cases.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD/PAB 250,000 — mandatory Local File is required for any Panamanian taxpayer (including a PIF) that carries out controlled or related-party transactions exceeding USD 250,000 in a given fiscal year. A Master File is mandatory where the multinational group's consolidated annual revenue equals or exceeds USD 50,000,000, or where cross-border related-party transactions exceed USD 2,000,000. Documentation must be filed with DGI within 6 months of the fiscal year-end and updated annually.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not operate a Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulation, but Law 254 of 2019 and its implementing decrees impose economic-substance reporting and effective-management requirements on entities carrying on 'relevant activities' (distribution, head-office, logistics, treasury, IP holding, and digital-commerce support). A PIF commercially managing a subscription-box business with fulfillment or distribution decisions in Panama must: (i) maintain physical premises or contracted fulfillment capacity in Panama, (ii) hold board council meetings in Panama with real decision-making minutes, (iii) employ or engage a Panama-based administrator or compliance officer, and (iv) file the annual economic-substance declaration through the CIGEx portal (Centro de Información de Sustancia Económica) identifying the nexus and employees. Failure to demonstrate substance may cause the DGI to deny a Tax Residence Certificate, reattribute foreign-source income as Panamanian-source, and expose the PIF to back assessments with interest and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting Panamanian-source subscription-box revenues from Form 42, fabricating deductions, or maintaining hidden Stripe Billing / Authorize.Net merchant accounts while falsely claiming territorial exclusion for Panama-based subscriber sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 100%–300% of the tax evaded plus monthly late-payment interest; under Law 66 of 2017, criminal prosecution applies where the evaded tax exceeds USD 50,000 in a fiscal year, carrying imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and fines equal to the evaded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The foundation council member, resident agent, or fiscal representative who signs the false return is jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax; personal travel bans (impedimento de salida), freezing of personal bank accounts, and extradition exposure attach upon indictment; courts may lift the PIF's legal shield and order civil restitution from directors' personal estates.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting forged supplier invoices, fabricated shipping and logistics records, fake subscriber lists, or false foreign-source certificates to substantiate the territorial exclusion and obtain a nil tax assessment or refund.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI may impose fines up to USD 250,000, cancel the RUC, revoke the resident agent's professional license, and refer the case to the Public Ministry; document forgery is punishable under the Panamanian Penal Code with 3 to 8 years' imprisonment and disqualification from commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, the foundation council, and the appointed Panamanian attorney/registered agent face criminal liability for forgery and making false declarations before a public authority, including imprisonment, civil restitution of the refunded or evaded tax, and professional disbarment; travel bans are routinely issued during the criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing subscription-box proceeds through Stripe Billing and Authorize.Net and related intermediary payment accounts to conceal beneficial ownership, structuring transactions to evade financial-intelligence thresholds, or commingling illicit funds with legitimate e-commerce revenue streams.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FIBA may impose administrative fines of USD 10,000 to USD 1,000,000 per infraction for violation of customer due diligence, record-keeping, and suspicious transaction reporting rules; money laundering as a predicate offense is punishable by 5 to 10 years' imprisonment, with aggravated penalties of up to 15 years for professional or cross-border laundering networks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Beneficiaries and directors convicted of laundering face imprisonment, civil and criminal forfeiture of the PIF's assets and personal assets, redesignation as OFAC/SDN targets where US payment rails are misused, and cross-border travel restrictions; directors who knowingly signed incomplete beneficial-ownership disclosures are personally liable for restitution and subject to asset freezing orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / False Economic Substance Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a passive PIF that nominally holds the subscription-box business, files zero or false CIGEx economic-substance declarations, and performs no real management, logistics, employment, or decision-making functions in Panama while claiming tax-free status for all revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Law 254 of 2019 carries administrative fines of up to USD 200,000 for false or materially incomplete substance declarations; the DGI may revoke the Tax Residence Certificate, reclassify the entire revenue stream as Panamanian-source, and assess the 10%/15%/25% CIT with statutory interest and a 100% negligence surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The foundation council and registered agent are personally liable for certifying false substance reports; sanctions include professional disqualification, civil restitution of the forgone tax amounts, travel bans during administrative or criminal recharacterization proceedings, and imprisonment for perjury or fraudulent misrepresentation where the false declaration exceeds the criminal threshold.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Veil Piercing and Director Personal Liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Abusing the PIF's separate juridical personality to strip assets, pay disguised dividends without the required 10%/5% withholding, undercapitalize the subscription-box operation while directors extract funds, or using the foundation as a mere alter ego of the non-resident beneficial owner to defeat creditors and tax claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panamanian courts may judicially lift the corporate veil under Law 32 of 1927 and the Judicial Code, consolidating the PIF's assets with the director/beneficiary's personal estate; the court may order reassessment of unpaid corporate income tax, the full dividend withholding tax, transfer-pricing adjustments, plus a 100% statutory surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners are held personally liable for civil restitution of the unpaid taxes and damages; travel bans are imposed pending the fraud investigation; imprisonment of 3 to 8 years applies for fraudulent misappropriation and fraud against the fisc, with additional penalties for using the PIF structure to obstruct tax collection.
